text:
emily_w: FYI support ticket #4891 — customer on Dedicated reporting sudden throughput drop, even though GPU utilization is low. Latency up, tail p50->p95 widening. Can someone triage?

support-jen: Customer says it started after a deploy around 06:12 UTC. They see 5x more small responses (50-100 tokens) and lots of backpressure errors. Attaching logs in ticket.

raj_k: grabbing the pool logs now. Which Dedicated pool?

support-jen: pool-id redwood-dedicated-us-west-2-42, tenant ACME-FF.

raj_k: I see many continuous-batcher yield events and frequent schedule preemptions in the sequencer logs. Looks like batch formation is timing out at micro-window and emitting tiny batches.

emily_w: Hmm that's consistent with their small responses spike. Any recent scheduler or max_batch_tokens changes?

thao_nguyen: We rolled the prefill->continuous-batcher tuning last night for mem/latency tradeoff: switched default max_batch_tokens from 4096 to 512 for certain pools to avoid OOM on quantized models. Could be related.

oncall-mike: alert: pool redwood-dedicated-us-west-2-42 autoscale flapped at 06:10-06:20 (scale down then up). Might have caused odd bundle placement.

raj_k: pasting a short snippet from sequencer.log around 06:13 — shows repeated micro-wakes:
```
[06:13:02] batcher: window_close timeout (5ms) - formed batch size=2 tokens=78
[06:13:02] batcher: prefilling=false continuous=true heat=low -> emit small batch
[06:13:03] scheduler: preempted by higher-priority tenant -> requeue calls
[06:13:05] batcher: re-wake due to kv-cache miss -> formed batch size=1 tokens=24
```

emily_w: Oof. That explains p95. Small batches mean GPU kernels warm-up overhead dominates. But why are batches timing out so quickly? Window_close set to 5ms is aggressive. Who changed that?

thao_nguyen: The canary for the new window heuristics adjusted micro-window to 5ms for low-heat workloads. It was targeted at inference latency for small chat clients, but apparently with this tenant's request patterns it fragments batches.

support-jen: Customer is very sensitive to token throughput — their SLA is throughput-based. They're already seeing billing anomalies reported (requests falling into retry loops).

raj_k: Also seeing many KV cache misses for this tenant, likely because of frequent model variant swaps (they route to a quantized variant). That forces prefill path and breaks batching synergy.

emily_w: Actionable plan: 1) revert micro-window to 20ms for this pool (temp) 2) pin max_batch_tokens back to 4096 for ACME-FF tenant routing rules 3) investigate autoscale flapping cause. Can we do 1 and 2 as a hotfix?

oncall-mike: I'll roll the pool config revert to 20ms now (will take ~30s). Pushing via ops-runbook edit: `opsctl pools update --id redwood-dedicated-us-west-2-42 --batch-window-ms 20`

infra-bot: deploy started by oncall-mike: opsctl pools update --id redwood-dedicated-us-west-2-42 --batch-window-ms 20 (run 0923b)

oncall-mike: rolled. Monitoring metrics: average batch size jumped from 1.8 -> 7.4 in the last 40s for tenant ACME-FF. p95 latency dropping slowly.

support-jen: I told the customer we applied a mitigation. They're running a test suite now.

thao_nguyen: I'll push a targeted tenant override change to restore max_batch_tokens=4096 for ACME-FF route. Command: `routerctl override set --tenant ACME-FF --max-batch-tokens 4096`

raj_k: After the revert and override, I still see occasional scheduler preemptions — need to confirm priority gating: ACME-FF was recently set to 'standard' priority; a noisy tenant on the same pool had transient bursts. Suggest adding soft isolation: cap concurrent microburst share for noisy tenant.

emily_w: Agree. For immediate customer relief, the window & max_batch_tokens revert should be enough. For long-term: add heuristic to continuous-batcher to prefer filling batches up to token threshold if the same tenant sends repeated small calls (tenant coalescing). Put a ticket in eng-runtime backlog.

raj_k: Filed ENGRT-7294: "tenant-coalesce heuristic for continuous-batcher" and assigned to me + thao.

support-jen: Customer test green: throughput returned to normal ~ 2.8x vs degraded, no immediate billing errors. They asked for a postmortem and confirmation this won't recur.

emily_w: Good. Next steps: (A) confirm autoscale flapping root cause (investigate instance termination logs) (B) create canary gating for micro-window heuristic (C) long-term batching heuristic. Who owns A?

oncall-mike: I'll take A, starting with autoscale event trace and cloud provider instance termination reasons.

thao_nguyen: I'll work on B/C with raj. We should also add a metric exposed in the console: "small_batch_ratio" per-tenant so support can triage faster.

emily_w: Perfect. I'll draft a short postmortem summary for the customer and ops runbook changes.

support-jen: Sending update to ticket now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: alert resolved: pool redwood-dedicated-us-west-2-42 batch-window reverted (run 0923b)
